lessons.title: Reading About Modern London
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about modern London from a text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about London today.
I can name a famous London landmark.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about London today.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a simple text about modern London landmarks (Big Ben, London Eye, Tower Bridge), modelling retrieval.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer retrieval questions and record a favourite landmark.
key_questions: What is London the capital of?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note retrieval skill applied to geography content — evidence for ENG.R2/GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Look up a London landmark together.

lessons.title: Counting Landmarks: Tally Charts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a tally chart to count and record data.
success_criteria: I can make a tally mark.
I can count tally marks to find a total.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting in groups.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a tally chart, counting in groups of 5.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a tally chart of favourite London landmarks voted on by the class, then total the results.
key_questions: How do you make a group of 5 tally marks?
Which landmark got the most votes?

differentiation.greater_depth: Interpret the completed chart, comparing totals

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early data handling skill — evidence for MATHS.N1/statistics links.
lessons.plenary: Recap the class's favourite landmark from the tally chart.
lessons.home_link: Create a simple tally chart of something at home (e.g. favourite fruits in the family).

lessons.title: How Has London Changed Since 1666?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way London has changed since the Great Fire.
success_criteria: I can name one change in London.
I can compare it to 1666 London.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what London was like in 1666.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Compare pictures of 1666 London to modern London, discussing key changes (buildings, transport, size).
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a then/now comparison for London using pictures and simple sentences.

differentiation.greater_depth: Give 3+ detailed comparisons

lessons.assessment_notes: Note historical comparison skill spanning centuries — evidence for HIST.1/HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how your local area might have changed over time.

lessons.title: Finding London on a Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to locate London on a map of the UK.
success_criteria: I can find London on a UK map.
I can say London is the capital city.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple UK map.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model locating London and discussing it as the capital city of England/the UK.
lessons.independent_task: Children locate and mark London on their own UK map outline.
key_questions: Where is London on the map?

differentiation.support: Adult points to London for child to mark
differentiation.greater_depth: Locate London and 1-2 other UK cities

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap London's location on the map.
lessons.home_link: Find London on a map or atlas at home.

lessons.title: Writing About a London Landmark
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about a London landmark.
success_criteria: I can name a landmark.
I can write a sentence describing it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap landmarks discussed on Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about a landmark (e.g. 'Big Ben is a tall clock tower.').
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 descriptive sentences about their favourite London landmark.
key_questions: What does your landmark look like?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied vocabulary

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share landmark descriptions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe a landmark to your family.

lessons.title: Two-Step Word Problems: A Day Out in London
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve two-step addition/subtraction word problems.
success_criteria: I can solve the first step of a problem.
I can use that answer for the second step.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap one-step word problems.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a two-step word problem (e.g. 'we see 5 landmarks, then 3 more, then visit 2 - how many left to see?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve 2-3 two-step word problems in a London day-out context.
key_questions: What do you do with that answer?

differentiation.support: Break into two separate one-step problems with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Solve independently and explain each step

lessons.assessment_notes: Note two-step problem-solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the steps used to solve two-step problems.
lessons.home_link: Make up a two-step problem for your family.

lessons.title: Transport Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare how people travelled in London then and now.
success_criteria: I can name a way people travelled in the past.
I can name a modern way to travel in London.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how people might have travelled in 1666 (walking, horse and cart, boat).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Compare historical transport to modern London transport (Underground, buses, bikes).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort transport picture cards into 'then' and 'now', or both.
key_questions: How do people travel in London today?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why transport has changed (technology, roads)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note change-over-time comparison skill — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how your family travels around today.

lessons.title: The Four Countries of the UK
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and locate the four countries of the UK.
success_criteria: I can name the four UK countries.
I can locate them on a map.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a UK map and discuss what children already know.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/recap the four countries of the UK and their rough locations.
lessons.independent_task: Children label the four UK countries on a map outline.
key_questions: What are the four countries of the UK?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add capital cities of each country

lessons.assessment_notes: Record locational knowledge of the UK — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Practise naming the four UK countries together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading London-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read London/landmark themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read landmark words.
I can read a sentence about London.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap graphemes practised this term.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending London-themed words.
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.

differentiation.greater_depth: Read sentences independently and fluently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading London words over the week.

lessons.title: Position and Direction: Map Journeys
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe position and direction using a simple map.
success_criteria: I can use words like left, right, forward.
I can follow a simple route on a map.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap left and right from earlier learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model following a simple route on a class floor map using directional language.
lessons.independent_task: Children follow and describe routes on a simple London-themed floor/paper map.

differentiation.greater_depth: Use left/right/forward combined instructions independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record positional/directional language use — evidence for MATHS.GEO/GEOG links.
lessons.home_link: Practise giving directions at home using left and right.

lessons.title: Buildings Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare building materials and styles then and now.
success_criteria: I can describe a 1666 building.
I can describe a modern building.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap 1666 wooden buildings.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Compare 1666 buildings to modern London skyscrapers, discussing material and height changes.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and compare a 1666 building and a modern building.
key_questions: What material is this building made from?
How tall is it compared to 1666 buildings?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add labels explaining material/height differences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note building comparison skill linking history and materials science — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Look at buildings near your home and guess how old they might be.

lessons.title: Capital Cities of the UK
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the capital cities of the four UK countries.
success_criteria: I can name London as England's capital.
I can name at least one other UK capital.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the four UK countries from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the capital cities of each UK country (London, Edinburgh, Cardiff, Belfast).
lessons.independent_task: Children match each UK country to its capital city on a map.
key_questions: What is the capital of Scotland?

differentiation.greater_depth: Match all 4 independently and locate on a map

lessons.assessment_notes: Record capital city knowledge — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Practise naming UK capital cities together.

lessons.title: Planning a Trip to London (Discussion)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss and justify what they would like to see on a trip to London.
success_criteria: I can say what I would like to see.
I can give a reason why.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap landmarks learned about this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model discussing and justifying a choice using 'because'.
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children discuss and justify which London landmarks they'd most like to visit.
key_questions: What would you like to see?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note discussion and justification skill — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Class vote on most popular landmark to visit.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family where you'd like to visit in London.

lessons.title: Reading and Interpreting a Simple Pictogram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to read and interpret a simple pictogram.
success_criteria: I can read how many a pictogram shows.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the tally chart from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model converting tally data into a simple pictogram and reading it.
lessons.independent_task: Children read a given pictogram (e.g. favourite landmarks) and answer questions about it.

differentiation.greater_depth: Create their own simple pictogram from data

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early data interpretation skill — evidence for MATHS.N1/statistics links.
lessons.home_link: Create a simple pictogram of a family survey at home.

lessons.title: What Would Surprise a 1666 Londoner Today?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to imagine and describe what might surprise someone from the past.
success_criteria: I can name something that would surprise a 1666 Londoner.
I can explain why.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key differences between 1666 and modern London discussed this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model imagining what might surprise a time-traveller from 1666 (cars, phones, tall buildings).
lessons.independent_task: Children write/draw what would surprise a 1666 Londoner about today and why.

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning for multiple surprises

lessons.assessment_notes: Note imaginative historical empathy and reasoning — evidence for HIST.1/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Share ideas about what would surprise a 1666 Londoner.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family what might surprise someone from 100 years ago.

lessons.title: Human vs Physical Features of London
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to distinguish between human and physical geographical features.
success_criteria: I can name a human feature (building, road).
I can name a physical feature (river, hill).
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the River Thames as a physical feature of London.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the distinction between human features (made by people) and physical features (natural).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort London feature picture cards into human and physical categories.
key_questions: Is this feature made by people or natural?
What physical feature runs through London?

differentiation.greater_depth: Sort independently and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record human/physical feature vocabulary — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap human and physical features of London.
lessons.home_link: Find a human and a physical feature near your home.

lessons.title: London Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about London then and now.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question about London.
I can answer a question comparing then and now.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's London vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a short passage about London then and now, modelling comprehension questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and comparison questions about the passage.

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing
differentiation.greater_depth: Answer comparison questions with full-sentence reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Read about London together if you have a book.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Data, Two-Step Problems, Position
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply data handling, problem-solving, and positional skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can read a tally chart/pictogram.
I can solve a two-step problem.
I can use positional language.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of data handling, two-step problems, and position/direction.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: How did you solve this problem?

differentiation.greater_depth: Independent completion with extension challenges

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 11 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising this week's maths skills over the weekend.

lessons.title: London Then and Now: Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about London then and now learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a change in London since 1666.
I can name something that has stayed similar.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's history and geography learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about London then and now.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'London Then and Now' display combining comparisons, maps, and drawings from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about London?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain multiple ideas with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, completing the Great Fire/London topic — evidence for HIST.1/HIST.2/GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about London with your family.

lessons.title: UK Geography Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall UK countries and capital cities learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name the four UK countries.
I can name their capital cities.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's geography vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quiz-style recap of UK countries and capitals.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a UK geography recap quiz/map activity.
key_questions: What are the four UK countries?
What is the capital of Wales?

differentiation.greater_depth: Complete independently with additional detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Record UK locational knowledge progress — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Practise naming UK countries and capitals over the weekend.
